scope: Shared Core C++ API; packaged Mac ARM64 Development Full Game clients and dedicated Server, loopback HTTP and ICE. Existing Blueprint lifecycle graphs also run; Blueprint data sample remains SR-106.
source_reuse_note: After the full build/test pipeline, only the client GC fixture changed. The client was rebuilt and repackaged. The Server package retains the earlier unused client-fixture methods; its Server probe and all production plugin sources match the repository and are unchanged. Both staged input manifests are hashed below. A final client recook added the existing Blueprint examples. All executable bytes outside LC_CODE_SIGNATURE are identical; the final re-signed package passed a fourth shared-session run and both lifecycle provider cases.

recook_binary_identity.note: The recook staged the same executable and re-signed the application. Bytes outside LC_CODE_SIGNATURE are identical.

added_coverage: Cancellation owns only its active attempt
Disconnect during Connect waits for teardown
Owner and PIE-world cleanup suppress callbacks
Garbage collection during direct cancellation cannot collect the dispatch owner
Channel state cannot regress after an early native Open sample
OpenChannel waits for the negotiated message limit

earlier_attempts.reason: Two unqualified MakeError calls collided with Unreal lookup; qualified before the successful builds.
The initial fixture tried to instantiate abstract UObject. Replaced it with UGameInstance.
Concurrent clients exposed a rejected send after successful OpenChannel.

The GC fixture incorrectly treated reference release as destruction. The final fixture releases its session outside callback dispatch and collects it while OpenChannel is pending, then checks for callbacks after actual collection.

Diagnostic reproduction showed Connected session, successful channel query and known limit, but channel no longer Open. Older Connecting notifications could overwrite Open; the game-thread adapter now prevents backward state changes.

The initial cook omitted the standalone Blueprint examples directory. Recooking with the documented -cookdir=Content/Examples argument fixed the packaged asset check; both C++/Blueprint provider cases then passed without code or asset changes.

limits: Mac ARM64 Full Game and dedicated Server only; Android/iOS, Windows/Linux, remote HTTPS, cross-device and NAT/TURN acceptance remain open.
Blueprint nodes share the implementation; this run validates real data through C++ and retains the earlier C++/Blueprint local lifecycle checks. Packaged Blueprint data flows remain SR-106.
PIE cleanup is an automation test with a PIE world cleanup delegate; the packaged real-peer case destroys a Game world. No interactive PIE network run is claimed.
Janus connections, calls, rooms, custom ICE server configuration, receive-only sessions, media and measured statistics remain unimplemented.
No network media, sustained-load, physical iOS or Shipping app-size qualification. M0 external acceptance gates remain open.
Existing Dawn linker warnings and minimal-host gameplay NetDriverCreateFailure do not establish failures in these HTTP/WebRTC probes. No engine source edits were made.
